title: Married filing jointly: the $242k Roth cliff

concepts.title: The line that matters: MAGI
concepts.body: Same MAGI line as single filers — modified adjusted gross income, not salary. The IRS Pub 590-A worksheet takes your AGI, adds back a few items, and that's the MAGI for Roth purposes.

concepts.title: MFJ phase-out: $242,000 to $252,000
concepts.body: Married filing jointly phases out from $242,000 to $252,000 in 2026. That's a ten-thousand-dollar window — narrower than the single filer window. The IRS worksheet reduces your allowed contribution inside that window.

concepts.title: Above $252,000: zero direct contribution
concepts.body: Above $252,000 in 2026, you cannot contribute directly to a Roth IRA. Zero. The direct-contribution door closes.

sources: IRS — 401(k) limit increases to $24,500 for 2026, IRA limit increases to $7,500 (IR-2025-111, Nov 13 2025)
